# Clauset

> Clauset is a free, open-source menu bar app and command for macOS. It runs several Claude Code accounts on one Mac, sharing one ~/.claude, shows each account's usage limits, and lets you move a running session to another account when a limit nears. It never switches accounts by itself.

## Pages

- [Clauset: Claude Code usage and multiple accounts on Mac](https://clauset.app/index.md): Clauset is a free menu bar app for macOS. See your Claude Code usage limits for every account, and move a running session to another when one nears.
- [Documentation](https://clauset.app/docs/index.md): The config file, how an account is picked, what's shared and what Clauset writes.
- [Changelog](https://clauset.app/changelog/index.md): What changed in each version of Clauset, the menu bar app and the command, newest first.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset): the app, the command and this site, under the MIT licence.

---

Source: https://clauset.app/

# Every Claude Code account, in your menu bar.

Clauset runs several Claude Code accounts on one Mac, sharing one `~/.claude`. See each account's usage limits, pick where new sessions start, and move a running session when a limit nears.

[Download for macOS](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset/releases/latest/download/Clauset.dmg) | [View on GitHub](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset)

Clauset is free and open source. It needs macOS 14.4 or later.

## One menu for every account.

Each account keeps its own sign-in and its own limits. Clauset shows them side by side and lets you choose which one works next.

### See every limit.

Each account shows its 5-hour window, its 7-day window and the weekly limit of one model, such as Fable. A bar turns orange from 70% and red from 90%.

### A warning before the limit.

Pick a threshold, for every account or for one. Clauset posts a notification when an account passes it, and another when it hits the limit.

### Move a session mid-work.

A session closes once its turn ends and resumes on the other account, in its own terminal. Background agents and teammates end with it.

### One setup, shared.

Settings, skills, plugins, MCP servers and memory come from one `~/.claude`. Only the sign-in differs.

### Pick where new sessions start.

Choose an account in the menu and every new `claude` starts there. A session started from another session stays on that session's account.

### It reads no token.

`clauset` makes no network call. Only the official `claude` binary talks to Anthropic. The app asks before it goes online, then checks GitHub for a newer version once a week.

## Set up in one window.

Every step says what it writes before you allow it: the `claude` shim, two hooks, a status line and two skills. Skip any you don't want.

## No terminal needed.

Adding an account, signing in again and moving sessions all run inside the app. A sign-in opens your browser, and a move asks first.

## Updates on your word.

A newer version shows in the menu and no window opens by itself. Choose to install, and the app downloads it from GitHub, checks its signature and opens again.

## The rest of it.

### Menu bar, your way

Follow the default account or pin one. Show the bars, the percentage, the name, or any mix.

### A limit per model

The weekly limit of one model, such as Fable, sits beside the two windows.

### Claude in Chrome

Name the account your browser extension is signed in to, and every other account reaches the same browser.

### Open at login

Clauset starts with your Mac and stays in the menu bar. It asks first.

### Doctor

Checks the shim, hooks, skills and status line, and every account's sign-in, Keychain item and links. It only reads.

### Status line

Every session shows the account it runs on, and keeps the usage the menu shows.

### Two skills

`/clauset` runs Clauset inside a session. `accounts` tells Claude what each command does and which ones wait for your word.

### A directory you already use

`clauset add --dir` takes in a config directory from another tool. Its sessions, memory and skills join the rest.

### For tools that start agents

`clauset run <account>` starts Claude Code on one account, from a terminal or a tool such as Solo.

### JSON for programs

`clauset status --json` gives every account with its sign-in, usage and sessions.

### Remove, and take back

Removing an account leaves its directory and sign-in, so adding it again brings it back.

### MIT licensed

The app and the command are one open repository. Read what it does before you run it.

## The command behind the menu.

The app reads and changes everything through `clauset`, and the command works without the app. Inside a session, `clauset switch work` moves it to another account.

To install the command without the app, with Homebrew:

```
$ brew trust mischasigtermans/tap
$ brew install mischasigtermans/tap/clauset-cli
$ clauset setup
```

Or with Cargo:

```
$ cargo install --locked --git \
https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset
$ clauset setup
```

```
$ clauset
~/code/app runs on personal  (the default)

→ personal  * Ultra  5h █░░░░░░░░░  12%  resets 14:00
                     7d ██░░░░░░░░  18%  resets Tue 09:00
                     me@example.com, personal | usage 4 min ago
  work        Team   5h ███░░░░░░░  31%  resets 13:00
                     7d ██████░░░░  61%  resets Sun 10:00
                     me@work.com, Acme | usage just now

$ clauset switch work
$ clauset use personal
```

## Questions, answered.

### Can I use multiple Claude Code accounts on one Mac?

Yes. Each account keeps its own sign-in in its own config directory, and they run side by side: one terminal on work, another on personal. Everything else is shared from one ~/.claude.

### How do I see my Claude Code usage?

The menu bar shows each account's 5-hour window, its 7-day window and the weekly limit of one model. The numbers come from what Claude Code itself stores, so an account shows them once a session has run on it.

### What happens when an account hits its usage limit?

Clauset posts a notification that names the account and when its limit resets. You can then move the running session to another account. Clauset never switches accounts by itself.

### Does it keep limits separate per account, or only switch logins?

Both. Every account keeps its own sign-in and its own limits, and Clauset shows each account's usage beside the others. Switching moves a session to another account and leaves every sign-in in place.

### Does Clauset read my tokens or send data anywhere?

It reads no token, and the command makes no network call. Only the official claude binary talks to Anthropic. The app asks before it goes online, then checks GitHub for a newer version once a week.

### Is Clauset free?

Yes. Clauset is free and open source under the MIT licence. It needs macOS 14.4 or later and Claude Code.

## Download Clauset.

Clauset is free and open source. It needs macOS 14.4 or later and Claude Code, signed in to at least one account.

[Download for macOS](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset/releases/latest/download/Clauset.dmg) | [View on GitHub](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset)

---

Source: https://clauset.app/docs/

# Configuration

`~/.claude/clauset/config.toml`, or the file `CLAUSET_CONFIG` names. Paths may start with `~/`. `clauset setup`, `add`, `remove`, `use`, `warn`, `chrome` and `switch` write it, keeping its comments, and refuse a change that would leave it invalid. What clauset records (usage, MCP server files, move requests), the shim's `bin/` and the menu bar app's `app.pid` and `notify/` sit in the same directory, which `link` leaves out of the accounts.

`clauset remove <account>` takes an account out of the file and drops its recorded usage. Its config directory and Keychain item stay, so `clauset add <account> --dir <dir>` takes it back. It refuses the default, the `chrome` account, the hub and an account sessions run on.

## Keys

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `default` | The account a session started from no clauset session runs on. `clauset switch` and `clauset use <account>` set it. |
| `warn_at` | Optional. The percent of a 5-hour or 7-day limit at which every account warns. `clauset warn 80` sets it. |
| `chrome` | Optional. The account the Claude in Chrome extension is signed in to. Every other account reaches the browser through it. `clauset chrome <name>` sets it, `clauset chrome off` removes it. |
| `[accounts.<name>] dir` | The account's config directory. `~/.claude` is the hub, which runs with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset, as Claude Code expects of its default directory. |
| `[accounts.<name>] email` | Optional. Prefilled at `clauset login`, checked by `doctor`. |
| `[accounts.<name>] warn_at` | Optional. This account's own threshold, over the global one. `clauset warn 60 --account <name>` sets it. |
| `[accounts.<name>] org` | Optional. The organization UUID the sign-in must belong to, checked by `login` and `doctor`. One login can belong to several organizations, picked in the browser. |

## Which account `claude` starts on

1. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names a directory no account owns: `claude` starts unchanged.
2. The process descends from a session clauset started (`CLAUSET_ACCOUNT` is set), or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names an account: that session's account.
3. The default.

`clauset which` prints the answer and the rule that gave it.

## What an account shares

Everything in the hub except what Claude Code keeps per account or org: `.claude.json` and its backups, the Keychain item, policy limits, remote settings, `daemon*`, `state/`, `chrome/`, `cache/`, `telemetry/`, `statsig/`, `feedback/`, `stats-cache.json` and a few more, listed in `src/link.rs`. `plugins/` stays apart too, because `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` points every account at the hub's, while Claude Code writes the plugins it syncs from claude.ai to `plugins/synced/<org>_<account>/` in each account's directory.

Shared on purpose: `projects/` (sessions and auto-memory), `history.jsonl` and `sessions/` (so `ListAgents` and `SendMessage` reach sessions on every account). A session started on one account resumes on another with `--resume <id>`.

MCP servers come from the hub: its user-scope ones and the directory's project-scope ones, written to `~/.claude/clauset/mcp/` in the shape `--mcp-config` reads and passed to every account beside the hub. A start with `--strict-mcp-config` gets none of them: the flag asks Claude Code for the caller's own `--mcp-config` alone. `claude mcp add` in a session on such an account writes to that account's own `.claude.json`, so add servers from a session on the hub; `doctor` names user-scope servers only one account has.

Claude in Chrome follows the `chrome` key. Claude Code reaches the browser extension through a relay that pairs a session only with extensions signed in to its own claude.ai account, so a session on another account finds no browser. With `chrome` set, clauset starts a session on every other account with `--no-chrome` and Claude Code's own Chrome server, `claude --claude-in-chrome-mcp`, run on the named account's sign-in from `~/.claude/clauset/mcp/chrome.json`. Claude Code keeps the name `claude-in-chrome` for its built-in server, so this one is called `chrome` and its tools `mcp__chrome__*`. The session still applies its own organization's Claude in Chrome policy. Claude Code keeps the preferred browser in the named account's `.claude.json`, so a browser picked with `select_browser` from any account holds for all of them. The named account itself, a config without `chrome`, and a start with `--chrome`, `--no-chrome` or `--strict-mcp-config` keep Claude Code's own handling.

`clauset link` links what the hub gained since; `doctor` reports a link Claude Code replaced with a file.

`clauset add <name> --dir <dir>` takes in a config dir that ran on its own. Signed in, it keeps its sign-in. A directory with files but no `.claude.json`, or one that holds your home directory, is refused before anything moves. Its own copies of shared directories move into the hub's wherever the hub has no entry of that name, so its sessions, memory and skills join the shared ones; what would clash, and its own copy of every shared file, stays in the directory as `<name>.before-clauset`.

## What `setup` and `add` write

`setup` asks before each step and leaves a step out when its files are already in place. For a program, `clauset setup --json` says which of the shim, the hooks, the status line and the skills are in place, and `clauset setup --apply <shim|hooks|statusline|skills>` puts one in place without asking. It leaves a status line of your own alone, and writes over a skill that differs only with `--replace`.

| Path | Written by | What |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.claude/clauset/config.toml` | `setup`, `add` | The accounts, the default and `warn_at`. |
| `~/.claude/clauset/bin/claude` | `setup` | A link to the clauset binary: the shim. |
| `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc` | `setup` | Two lines at the end: a comment and `export PATH="<home>/.claude/clauset/bin:$PATH"`, so the shim comes before every other `claude`. Another shell gets the line printed to add by hand. |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | `setup` | The `SessionStart` and `StopFailure` hooks below, and the `statusLine` when there's none. The file is written back whole, as JSON indented by two spaces, its keys in their order. |
| `~/.claude/skills/clauset/SKILL.md` | `setup` | The `/clauset` skill, as shipped in `skills/clauset/SKILL.md`. |
| `~/.claude/skills/accounts/SKILL.md` | `setup` | The `accounts` skill, as shipped in `skills/accounts/SKILL.md`. |
| `~/.claude-accounts/<name>/` | `add`, `login` | A new account's config directory, with a link into the hub for every shared entry. `add --dir` uses the directory you name. |
| `.claude.json` of an account beside the hub | `add`, `login`, `link`, `switch` | Onboarding, theme, the one-time dialogs the hub has answered, and the trust of every project the hub trusts. Keys the account has keep their values. |
| `~/.claude/` | `add --dir` | The entries the taken-in directory has and the hub lacks. |

The Keychain item and the account's sign-in in its `.claude.json` come from `claude auth login`, which `add` and `login` start. Claude Code keeps one sign-in per config directory, so a new one changes the account under every session running there. For the hub, where a `claude` started outside clauset runs too, `login` therefore waits until no session runs on it.

## Moving a session

A Claude Code process keeps the config directory it started with, so a session moves to another account by ending and resuming there. At a terminal the shim and `clauset run` keep `claude` as a child under a supervisor, and `clauset switch <account>`, run inside the session as `/clauset switch <account>`, `! clauset switch <account>` or by Claude, asks that supervisor to move it. It also makes the account the default, so new sessions start there too.

1. The session finishes its turn. Once Claude Code's session registry says it's idle and it runs no background shell, the supervisor ends it.
2. The supervisor starts `claude --resume <session id>` on the other account in the same terminal, with the flags that shape the session (permissions, model, effort, agent, settings, system prompt, added directories, tools, name); its prompt and the flags that pick a session stay behind. An account beside the hub also gets the trust the first account gave the directory; the hub's `.claude.json` is left to the sessions that write it.

Background shells would end with the session, so the move waits until they have stopped: a watcher that never ends holds it until it's stopped through `/tasks`. `clauset switch` to the account the session runs on cancels a move it asked for and makes that account the default. A refused switch, from a session without the supervisor, leaves the default as it was. Background agents and teammates run inside the session and end with it. The first turn on the other account reads the whole conversation again, without the thinking written under the other organization. A session that ends on its own before it moves stays ended.

`clauset switch <account> --all` moves every session on the account being left, not only the one it runs in: the account the enclosing session runs on, or the one `--from <account>` names, which a terminal outside a session needs. Each supervisor notes the account its `claude` runs on in `~/.claude/clauset/supervised/<pid>.json` and removes the note when `claude` ends, since macOS keeps a process's environment from other processes. `--all` writes the request of every session whose supervisor runs it on that account, and each moves as above, once its own turn ends and its background shells have stopped; the output names the busy ones and those that wait for a shell. It makes the account the default once, and only when at least one session will move. A second `--all` writes the same requests again, so a session waiting to move keeps its place and gets only the newest target. A terminal session without a supervisor note, from a supervisor older than this version among others, stays where it is: the output lists it with the `clauset run <account> --resume <id>` that moves it by hand, since clauset can't tell its account. Sessions that Claude Code started for an SDK or another tool are left out.

MCP servers that sign in with OAuth, and the claude.ai connectors of an account's organization, keep their sign-in per account. On the account a session moves to they may need a sign-in through `/mcp`; clauset reads no token, so it can't tell beforehand.

A session that runs without the supervisor, because stdin was no terminal or it started before clauset, moves by hand: end it and run `clauset run <account> --resume <id>`. `/login` inside a session signs in the config directory itself, so it changes the account of every session that runs on it.

## Skills

`setup` writes two skills into the hub's `skills/`, so every account has them:

- `clauset`: `/clauset <args>` runs clauset in the session. Its body holds the line ``!`clauset $ARGUMENTS 2>&1 || true` ``, which Claude Code runs itself before the model reads the skill, since its frontmatter has `allowed-tools: Bash(clauset:*)`. Its `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps the model from invoking it with arguments of its own. It finds `clauset` on PATH; when it's missing there, the skill tells you how to install it.
- `accounts`: tells Claude which clauset commands it may run itself (`clauset`, `which`, `doctor`), which wait for your word, how to move a session, and how to install clauset when it's missing.

`doctor` warns about a missing skill and notes one that differs from the shipped one. `setup` writes a missing skill, and offers to replace one that differs, since you may have changed it on purpose.

The install command both skills name is `cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset`; the source is at [github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset](https://github.com/mischasigtermans/clauset).

## Usage

`clauset` shows each account's use of its 5-hour and 7-day limits from two places Claude Code fills itself, whichever is fresher:

- `cachedUsageUtilization` in the account's `.claude.json`, written each time Claude Code fetches the account's usage.
- The `rate_limits` Claude Code hands a status line command, which `clauset statusline` keeps per account in `~/.claude/clauset/usage/`. Claude Code sends them for subscription plans, Team included.

An account shows numbers once a session has run on it; the overview says how old they are. A window Claude Code leaves out is left out of the overview too: a plan without a 5-hour limit shows its 7-day bar alone. A bar is blue, yellow from 70% and red from 90%.

A weekly limit that counts one model alone, such as Fable's, is only in `cachedUsageUtilization`: a status line gets no such limit. The overview shows it on the line under the bars with its own age, which is the time since Claude Code last fetched the account's usage, often a day or more.

With `warn_at` set, `clauset statusline` puts up a macOS notification the first time a window passes it, once per window: after the reset it may warn again. The `StopFailure` hook adds one when an account hits its limit, with every other account's fullest window beside it. clauset never moves work to another account on a limit; the notification leaves that choice to you. Both notifications look at the 5-hour and 7-day windows alone: a model's own weekly limit is too old a number to warn on.

The menu bar app writes its process id to `app.pid`. While that process runs, clauset leaves a notification as a file in `notify/`, a directory only you can write to, and the app posts it under its own name. Without the app, or when it has no permission to notify, AppleScript puts it up.

## Hooks and status line

In the hub's `settings.json`, shared by every account, with the path of the clauset binary `setup` ran from (`~/.cargo/bin/clauset` after `cargo install`):

```json
"SessionStart": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.cargo/bin/clauset hook context", "timeout": 5}]}],
"StopFailure": [{"matcher": "rate_limit", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "~/.cargo/bin/clauset hook limit", "timeout": 5}]}]
```

`setup` gives a hook with another matcher, or one that runs a clauset installed elsewhere, the current one, and `doctor` reports it.

A status line command pipes the JSON Claude Code hands it through `clauset statusline`, which prints the account and keeps its usage. When there's no status line, `setup` writes `"statusLine": {"type": "command", "command": "~/.cargo/bin/clauset statusline"}`, and offers to point one that runs another clauset's `statusline` at its own. Any other status line it leaves alone and names the pipe to add.

## Solo

[Solo](https://soloterm.com) is a terminal app that starts agents from agent tools. One agent tool per account: command `~/.cargo/bin/clauset`, arguments `run <account> --dangerously-skip-permissions`, tool type `claude` set by hand so resume keeps working. The stock Claude Code tool starts on the default once the shim is on PATH.

## Undocumented behaviour clauset relies on

- The Keychain item of a config directory is `Claude Code-credentials-` and the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its resolved path. `doctor` checks each one exists.
- Claude Code gives every process its tools start `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, keeps each interactive session's `status` (`busy`, `idle`) in `sessions/<pid>.json`, starts each Bash tool shell from `<config dir>/shell-snapshots/snapshot-*`, and ends a session cleanly on SIGTERM. `clauset switch` rests on all four.
- Each entry in `sessions/<pid>.json` holds the `sessionId`, `name`, `cwd` and `entrypoint` (`cli` for a terminal session) of a running session, and `procStart`, its process's start time as `ps -o lstart=` prints it in UTC; clauset accepts it in the C locale or the inherited one. `clauset switch --all` finds the sessions to move there and leaves out an entry whose pid now belongs to a process started at another time.
- `.claude.json` keeps `cachedUsageUtilization`, and `oauthAccount.planDisplayName` for personal plans (`Ultra`); a Team organization has no display name.
- Claude in Chrome reaches the extension only through a relay keyed on the session's claude.ai account, and its server is `claude --claude-in-chrome-mcp`, a switch `claude --help` doesn't list. `--mcp-config` refuses a local server named `claude-in-chrome` and accepts one named `chrome`. The `chrome` key rests on all three. If an update drops the switch, `/mcp` lists the `chrome` server as failed. If it reserves `chrome` too, the server is left out with only a line in the debug log. Either way, sessions on accounts other than the one `chrome` names have no browser until they start with `--chrome` or the key is removed.

---

Source: https://clauset.app/changelog/

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

**Added**

- `clauset status --json` gives every account with its sign-in, usage, warning threshold and number of supervised sessions, plus the default and `chrome`, for a program to read.
- The overview shows an account's weekly limit per model, such as Fable's, with how old that number is: it comes from Claude Code's own cache alone.
- `clauset setup --json` says what each setup step still needs, and `clauset setup --apply <shim|hooks|statusline|skills>` carries one out without asking. `--apply skills --replace` also writes this version's skill over one that differs.
- `clauset chrome <account|off>` sets or removes the `chrome` key.
- `clauset remove <account>` takes an account out of the config and leaves its directory and sign-in. It refuses the default, the `chrome` account, the hub and an account sessions run on.
- While the menu bar app runs, notifications come through it, under its name.
- The menu bar app updates itself through Sparkle. It asks the first time it opens. With your yes it fetches its release feed from GitHub once a week, shows a newer version in the menu and installs it when you choose to. `clauset` itself still makes no network call.

**Changed**

- `clauset login` signs the hub in again once no session runs on it. It refused the hub outright, and left it to `claude auth login`.
- The overview leaves out a window an account doesn't have, where it wrote `no 5h window`.
- A usage bar is blue, yellow from 70% and red from 90%. It was green, yellow from 50% and red from 80%.
- A notification names an account as the menu bar app shows it: `steddle-1` reads `Steddle 1`. It gave the name as the config has it.
- Clauset in `macos/`, a menu bar app that shows every account's usage, sets the default, the warning thresholds and `chrome`, and moves sessions between accounts. It reads and changes everything through clauset.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-11-16

**Added**

- A `chrome` key names the account the Claude in Chrome extension is signed in to. Every other account reaches that browser through it, as the `chrome` MCP server.

## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-13

**Fixed**

- `--strict-mcp-config` works on an account beside the hub. clauset added the hub's servers through `--mcp-config` on every start, so a caller who asked for its own servers alone still got all of the hub's.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-13

**Added**

- A `claude` shim that starts Claude Code on the account of the session that started it, else on the default.
- The shim leaves a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` that names no account untouched, and starts `claude` unchanged without a config.
- `clauset` (or `clauset usage`) shows the account here and every account's plan, sign-in and use of its 5-hour and 7-day limits, from Claude Code's own `cachedUsageUtilization` and the status line's `rate_limits`.
- `clauset setup` names the hub's account, suggesting a name after its organization.
- `clauset setup` signs in more accounts.
- `clauset setup` asks which account new sessions start on.
- `clauset setup` installs the shim, the hooks, the status line and the `clauset` and `accounts` skills, asking before each step.
- `clauset setup` points hooks and a status line that run a clauset installed elsewhere at its own, and replaces a skill that differs from the shipped one only when you say so.
- `clauset setup` asks for a warning threshold once the status line runs `clauset statusline`.
- `clauset use <account>` sets the default, keeping the config's comments.
- `clauset add` signs in a new account.
- `clauset add --dir` takes in an existing config dir, folding its sessions, memory and skills into the hub.
- Accounts beside the hub use the hub's plugins through `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`.
- Accounts beside the hub get the hub's user-scope and project-scope MCP servers through `--mcp-config`, from files that hold only the servers.
- `clauset hook context` on `SessionStart` gives the model its account.
- `clauset statusline` prints the account and keeps its usage.
- `clauset warn <percent|off> [--account]` sets `warn_at`, and the status line notifies once per window when an account passes it.
- `clauset hook limit` on `StopFailure` notifies when an account hits its limit.
- `clauset switch <account>` moves a session the shim or `clauset run` started at a terminal to another account once its turn ends, resuming it with `--resume` in the same terminal with the flags that shape it.
- `clauset switch <account>` makes the account the default for new sessions.
- `clauset switch` waits for the session's background shells to stop before it moves it, and refuses a session without the supervisor, leaving the default as it was.
- `clauset switch` to the session's own account cancels a move.
- `clauset switch <account> --all [--from <account>]` moves every supervised session on the account being left, names the sessions it can't move with the command that moves them by hand, and makes the account the default once.
- The `/clauset <args>` skill runs clauset inside a session.
- The `accounts` skill tells Claude what each clauset command does and which ones wait for the user.
- Both skills name the install command when `clauset` isn't found.
- `clauset run <account>` starts Claude Code on one account.
- `clauset login <account>` signs an account in again.
- `clauset doctor` checks the shim, the hooks, the skills, the status line, and every account's sign-in, Keychain item and links.
- `clauset which` names the account `claude` starts on here, and why.
- `clauset link` links what the hub gained since into the accounts.
